narrative.overview:
BrickFill is a workbench, not a showroom. The curator works the day's queue at a desk, and every screen is laid out
so a value sits next to its proof: the source page, the screenshot, the crop, the rule it passed or failed. The
surface stays calm and warm, with paper-toned backgrounds, Ink text and thin outlines, so the evidence and the few
decisions that matter stand out. Its character is **sober and precise**: tool density, thin borders, softly rounded
corners, and color only where it says something.

The system is built on Databricks AppKit UI (shadcn components on Tailwind v4) and themed through its CSS variables
in `app/brickfill/client/src/index.css`. The brand lives in precise details:

- the terracotta Kiln on the one action that moves the work forward;
- the brick-course mark that fills from the bottom up;
- warm Mortar neutrals instead of cold grays.

It has two confirmed anti-references:

- the "AI magic" panel, whose glows, gradients and sparkles sell the model instead of showing the evidence;
- the dense gray ERP, where every row and label has the same weight and nothing breathes.
keyCharacteristics: Paper and Ink with warm Mortar neutrals; Kiln (terracotta) is used only for actions and the current selection.
Four status tones (success, warning, info, danger), each a soft surface with same-hue text, always shown with an icon and a label.
Flat surfaces separated by hairlines; shadows are minimal and grow only on what floats.
The system sans in a clear, short scale; tabular numerals in every figure.
Light and dark themes with their own values (the dark theme is not the light one inverted), and an optional customer accent that replaces only Kiln.

rules.name: The Kiln Is for Doing Rule
rules.body: Kiln marks the action that moves the work forward and the user's current place. Nothing that only describes state is drawn in Kiln, so a reviewer always knows where to click.

rules.name: The Never Color Alone Rule
rules.body: Every status carries an icon and a word next to its tone: CircleCheck for approved, TriangleAlert for review, CircleX for rejected, and so on. A grayscale screenshot must still be readable.

rules.name: The Twin Dark Rule
rules.body: The dark palette is written twice in `index.css`, once for a `.dark` class and once for the system setting. `theme.test.ts` fails if the two differ, so change both together.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: A heading speaks for itself; no small colored kicker sits above it. The page eyebrows were removed in the polish pass and must not come back.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Percentages, counts, page numbers and step numbers use tabular numerals so columns and neighboring metrics line up.

rules.name: The Hairline First Rule
rules.body: Separate with a 1px Hairline or a tone step before reaching for a shadow. A shadow means "this floats", and nothing that sits in the page floats.

dos: Do keep Kiln for the primary action, the active navigation item, focus and selection; one filled Kiln button per area.
Do pair every status tone with its icon and label, and use the soft surface with same-hue text from the status tones.
Do give fields the Field Outline (≥3:1) and keep Hairline for decoration only.
Do use tabular numerals for every figure, and the system sans at the scale above.
Do make touch targets 44px on coarse pointers, and turn tables into labeled stacked blocks below 1024px.
Do change `.dark` and the `prefers-color-scheme: dark` block together; `theme.test.ts` checks that they match.
donts: Don't add glows, gradients, sparkle effects or gradient text to sell the AI. Show the evidence instead. The "AI magic" panel is a confirmed anti-reference.
Don't flatten every row, label and figure to the same gray weight; the dense gray ERP is a confirmed anti-reference.
Don't put an eyebrow or kicker above a heading.
Don't draw a status in Kiln, or use a new hue for a status outside the four tones.
Don't nest cards, add colored side or top stripes, or use a shadow on anything that does not float.
Don't add a webfont or a display face; the brand lives in the wordmark's weight and the mark.
